gaps: A whitespace-only variant query has no defined behavior: it may count as a variant search and create two groups, or become an empty query and match every card. Specify whether the query is trimmed before deciding that a variant was entered (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:24, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:28-35).
Results have no stated ordering when the member leaves variant blank; alphabetical order is specified only within the two groups used for a variant search (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:31-38).

The spec does not say how to handle a holder with both a matching stated variant and a card with no variant. That holder qualifies for both groups, while each person must appear once; the group assignment and which cards appear on that person's result are undefined (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:31-38, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:85-87).

A search is a snapshot, but the spec does not say what happens to an already displayed result or its contact button when the card is edited or removed, the holder leaves a shared circle, or the searcher is removed. Adjacent contracts require those changes to end visibility immediately, including through direct requests (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:39-40, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:52-60, docs/specs/cards.md:75-87, docs/specs/circles.md:79-89).

The browse flow does not explicitly require its member-card data request and contact action to check current shared membership. Search has a direct-request protection criterion, but browse has none, leaving a path to a former circle member's cards or number after access ends (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:47-49, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:88-99, docs/specs/accounts.md:88-96).

The search event's people-found value is undefined for the owner’s per-circle counts when one holder shares several circles with the searcher. It also does not say how a search by a member in no circles is counted. The accepted decision requires counts per circle (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:43-45, docs/decisions/0008-first-party-usage-counters.md:16-19).

The spec does not define whether a WhatsApp tap is recorded before navigation, or what the member sees if event recording fails. That leaves an implementation choice between losing a counted tap and blocking the core contact flow (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:52-61, docs/decisions/0008-first-party-usage-counters.md:21-24).

A member's WhatsApp number is self-entered and unverified. The spec does not define the contact experience when the number has no WhatsApp account or WhatsApp cannot open, although the acceptance criterion promises an opened chat (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:52-58, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:91-93, docs/decisions/0007-google-signin-whatsapp-number.md:15-22).
contradictions: The label "Exact variant" describes a full match, while the required matching rule is a case-insensitive substring match. A card named "Regalia Gold" would be labelled exact for a query of "Regalia" (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:28-35, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:81-84).

Acceptance criterion 1 says a search returns exactly every holder with the chosen bank and type, but criterion 3 excludes holders whose stated variant differs when a variant is entered. Criterion 1 needs the variant condition to avoid opposing expected results (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:76-84).

The contact event identifies its actor as "the searcher", but the member-list browse flow offers the same contact button without any search. The required event actor is therefore undefined for a supported route to contact (docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:47-49, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:59-60, docs/specs/find-and-contact.md:94-99).
resolutions: The variant entry is trimmed first; empty after trimming means no variant.
Without a variant, results are one list alphabetical by display name.
A person appears once: under Matching variant if any card matches, otherwise Variant not stated; all qualifying cards are shown.
Contact re-checks card existence and shared membership at press time and shows 'This card is no longer available.' otherwise; new searches show current state.
Added Enforcement: search, browse and contact check shared membership per request; browse covered by AC6.
People found counts distinct people once regardless of circles or cards; a searcher with no circles is recorded with no circle.
Recording never delays or blocks opening WhatsApp; a failed record leaves the tap uncounted (taps are a proxy per decision 0008).
The button opens WhatsApp's chat link; the app cannot tell whether the number is on WhatsApp, and WhatsApp's own screen explains failures.
Renamed the group to 'Matching variant' to fit the contains rule.
AC1 now states both the no-variant and variant conditions.
The tap event's actor is the member who pressed, from search or browse.

artifact_delta.cold:
- A card matches when its bank is the chosen bank, its type fits the chosen
  type, and, if a variant was entered, its variant contains the entered text,
  ignoring case and surrounding spaces.
- When a variant was entered, results come in two labelled groups:
  1. "Exact variant": cards whose variant matches;
  2. "Variant not stated": cards of that bank and type with no variant
     recorded, because the holder may still have the right card.
  Cards with a different, stated variant are not shown.
- Each result is one person, showing their display name, their matching cards
  (bank, type, variant) and the names of the circles the searcher shares with
  them. Within each group, people are listed alphabetically by display name.
- Results reflect cards and memberships as they are at the moment of the
  search.
artifact_delta.final:
- Without a variant, a card qualifies when its bank is the chosen bank and its
  type fits the chosen type. Results are one list, alphabetical by display
  name.
- With a variant, a card of the chosen bank and type qualifies when either:
  - its variant contains the entered text, ignoring case (a "matching
    variant"); or
  - it has no variant recorded, because the holder may still have the right
    card.
  Cards with a different, stated variant do not qualify. Results come in two
  labelled groups, each alphabetical by display name:
  1. "Matching variant": people with at least one matching-variant card;
  2. "Variant not stated": people whose only qualifying cards have no variant.
- Each result is one person, shown once, with their display name, all their
  qualifying cards (bank, type, variant) and the names of the circles the
  searcher shares with them.
- Results reflect cards and memberships at the moment of the search. A new
  search always shows the current state.

**Enforcement**
- Search results, a browsed member's cards and the contact action each check
  shared membership at the time of the request. Data about a person the
  requester no longer shares a circle with is never returned, including
  through direct data requests.
- Checking whether a number is registered on WhatsApp.
